checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: expose the camera path library's existing rename and duplicate through the editor API - rename_camera_path and duplicate_camera_path actions (editor schema 66) taking name plus new_name, mapping collisions to 400 and missing entries to 404, refreshing camera_path_document under the new name, console Path name/New name inputs with Rename and Duplicate buttons, web schema examples and required fields, tests and docs

impact_assessment.why: CameraPathLibrary has supported rename and duplicate since it shipped, but the editor and console could not reach them while state machines expose both actions, so a copied cutscene route required saving a new JSON document by hand.
impact_assessment.benefits: Camera paths reach lifecycle parity with clips and state machines: an authored route can be renamed or forked from the console and API without touching files, and the panel keeps editing the new entry.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two editor actions, editor schema 66, a new console input and two buttons; dependency: server reuses CameraPathLibrary rename/duplicate; concurrency: unchanged session lock; state: no scene, snapshot or render format change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Reuse the library's collision and traversal guards, pin success, collision, missing-entry and missing-library behaviour in web tests, keep one web schema example per action, smoke the panel in a browser, and verify the canonical hash and reference PNG unchanged

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - editor schema 66 adds rename_camera_path and duplicate_camera_path (name plus new_name) delegating to CameraPathLibrary, mapping a live target to 400 with a choose-another-name fix, a missing source to 404, an identical duplicate to 400 with a differs fix while an unchanged rename is a no-op, and refreshing camera_path_document under the resulting name; the console adds a New name input and Rename/Duplicate buttons; web schema examples and required fields cover both actions; README, AI_GUIDE, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and ADR-266 updated; one new web test pins rename, duplicate, collision, identical duplicate, missing source, blank and traversal names and the missing-library fix; browser smoke renamed intro to opening and duplicated to opening-copy with the panel following the new document; full pytest and ruff pass, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged

Task 'keystone-camera-path-rename-v1' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: play a camera path in the console - a Play path/Pause path button that advances preview_camera_path time with the same capped 33ms tick used by animation preview, reapplying the sampled pose to the scene view camera, wrapping for looping paths, stopping at the duration for one-shot paths, halting on any editor action, and updating the path readout without clobbering the JSON editor

impact_assessment.why: The console could sample a single camera path pose but not watch the authored move, so a cutscene route had to be scrubbed one time value at a time while animation clips already had a real playback button.
impact_assessment.benefits: Authors see the actual spline, lens and heading behavior in the viewport, loop and one-shot playback match the runtime player semantics, and nothing new is needed in the API because preview_camera_path already samples arbitrary times.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: console-only, no editor schema or API change; dependency: reuses preview_camera_path and the existing bookmark pose application; concurrency: one in-flight tick guarded by a busy flag; state: no scene, snapshot or render format change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Mirror the proven animation playback loop, stop playback on every editor action, pin the controls and handlers in the static console test, smoke play, pause and auto-stop in a browser, and keep the canonical hash and reference PNG unchanged

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - the console path panel gains Play path/Pause path backed by preview_camera_path on the animation preview loop (33ms timer, busy guard, 0.2s clamped ticks), wrapping looping paths, stopping one-shot paths at duration with the final pose applied, halting on every editor action, and refreshing a readout extracted into renderCameraPathState so ticks never re-render the hierarchy or the JSON editor; README, AI_GUIDE, CHANGELOG and ADR-267 updated; the static console test pins camera-path-play and the playback handler names; browser smoke played a two-key two-second path from 0 to 2 with the end pose 4.00, 1.50, 4.00, paused at 0.672 and held the time, and auto-stopped at the end; full pytest and ruff pass, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged

[3/3] UI review recorded - ui begin/verify/finish --reviewed closed the web surface as a no-change review of 1630f6a after a live browser pass (play to the end pose, pause froze the clock, auto-stop at the one-shot duration), and the review record is committed as 23b0764
Task 'keystone-camera-path-playback-v1' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 23b076462bcc7f458c5edc8f44a652abe737c074

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: drive deterministic evidence captures from a camera path - camera_path_route(path, frames, name, checkpoints, step) in evidence.py builds a Route whose stage samples the path at (frame-1)*step and assigns pose.to_camera(scene.camera), defaulting to one final checkpoint, so capture_route renders authored moves without games hand-rolling a clock; exports, tests, docs and ADR

impact_assessment.why: Camera paths and deterministic capture routes are both engine strengths, but they could not compose: an authored cutscene move had no way to become an evidence artifact, and every game would rebuild the per-frame camera staging and the 1/60 step convention.
impact_assessment.benefits: A cutscene or AI-authored camera move becomes a reproducible capture plan in one call, loops and one-shot durations follow CameraPath.sample semantics, the authored near/far range is preserved through pose.to_camera, and evidence diffs can compare authored camera moves byte for byte.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one new helper and export, no format change; dependency: evidence gains a camera_path import with no cycle; concurrency: the engine still runs single-threaded; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate the path type and step, delegate frame, name and checkpoint rules to Route, pin staging positions, loop wrap, clamping, defaults, near/far preservation and a real rendered difference in tests, and keep the canonical hash and reference PNG unchanged

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - evidence.py gains camera_path_route(path, frames, name, checkpoints, step) which validates the path and step, delegates frame/name/checkpoint rules to Route, stages pose.to_camera(scene.camera) at (frame-1)*step, preserves near/far, defaults to one final checkpoint and leaves loop wrap or one-shot clamping to CameraPath.sample; exported from the package and documented in the AI guide evidence section, FEATURES, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and ADR-268; seven tests in tests/test_evidence.py pin defaults, custom checkpoints, staging positions, lens depth, loop wrap, validation and a real headless capture whose first and last image hashes differ; full pytest and ruff pass, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged
Task 'keystone-camera-path-evidence-v1' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 77b60fd9d5580813ff11983c5eeec689b1104c4f

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: blend two camera poses for cutscene transitions and close the camera path discovery gap - CameraPose.blend(other, factor) lerps position and lens and slerps orientation with strict validation, capabilities gain camera_pose_blend and the already-shipped camera_path_route evidence helper, plus tests, docs and ADR

impact_assessment.why: Cutscenes need to move smoothly between two authored camera states, and the engine could only snap: CameraShaker composes offsets but nothing interpolates between poses. The camera path evidence helper also shipped without a discovery flag, so AI clients cannot see it from --describe.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games get a tested, deterministic pose transition that composes with camera paths, rigs and the shaker, and the capability block now names both the blend primitive and the camera-path evidence route.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one new method and two capability flags, no format change; dependency: camera_path only; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate the other pose and factor strictly, pin endpoints, midpoint position, orientation and lens, wrap and mirrored-quaternion behaviour, and the two discovery flags, then verify the canonical hash and reference PNG unchanged

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - CameraPose.blend(other, factor) validates a CameraPose target and a finite factor in [0,1], lerps position and fov, slerps normalized orientations through the shortest arc and returns a new frozen pose; capabilities gain camera_pose_blend and the missing camera_path_route flag; README, FEATURES, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and ADR-269 updated; five blend tests pin endpoints, midpoint position/lens/heading, mirrored quaternions, validation and camera composition plus immutability, and the two discovery tests pin the new flags; full pytest and ruff pass, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged
Task 'keystone-camera-pose-blend-v1' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: scrub camera paths on a console timeline - a range input mirroring the animation timeline that follows the preview time, sets its max from the previewed path duration, stops playback while dragging and previews the chosen time on release

impact_assessment.why: The animation panel has a timeline slider, but camera paths only accept a typed time, so reviewing a cutscene move means repeated typing while the authored duration is invisible.
impact_assessment.benefits: Authors drag through the move and see each pose in the viewport, looped and one-shot durations are explicit in the slider range, and playback, the time field and the slider stay in sync.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: console-only, no API or schema change; dependency: reuses preview_camera_path; concurrency: unchanged single tick loop; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Mirror the proven animation scrub wiring, keep the slider read-only during playback, pin the control and sync handler in the static console test, smoke dragging in a browser, and keep the canonical hash and reference PNG unchanged

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - the camera path panel gains a Timeline range input (camera-path-scrub) whose max follows camera_path_preview.path.duration and whose value follows the preview time; dragging stops playback and writes the time field, release previews the chosen time through preview_camera_path, and playback moves the slider with the clock; syncCameraPathTimeline is called from renderCameraPathState; README, AI_GUIDE, CHANGELOG and ADR-270 updated; the static console test pins the slider id and sync handler; browser smoke previewed a two-key two-second path (max 2) and scrubbed to 1, previewing the midpoint pose 2.00, 1.50, 6.00; full pytest and ruff pass, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged
